_descriptor_type: A type of descriptor. One of 'simulation', 'trace', and 'perf'.
_architecture: A name of the available architectures (PARAMS.<architecture>) found in scarab repository, which defines the machine parameters of the default configuration.
_experiment: The name of the experiment. scarab-infra will create a new folder named containing all files needed to execute the simulation in the <ROOT_DIR>/simulations/<experiment> directory. The folder will also contain all generated simulation statistics/outputs.
_workload_manager: manual: run each exp scenario with all the simpoints at a time, slurm: Slurm schedules simulations based on its policy
_root_dir: Root directory mounted into the docker container home, for instance, the user's home directory
_application_dir: The path to the benchmark application directory used for tracing or simulation.
_scarab_path: The path to the scarab repository that contains the scarab binary used to run the experiment. MUST be a build containing the mlc_fill_line ordering fix (victim selection + writeback moved BEFORE cache_insert, matching l1_fill_line). That fix roughly HALVES the RRPV aging rate at the MLC -- pre-fix, srrip_update_evict ran a full aging normalization twice per fill (once inside cache_insert, once again from the trailing get_next_repl_line on a set that no longer had a line at RRIP_DISTANT_VAL); post-fix it runs once. Aging is the only thing that erodes marked-RRIP's negative insertion RRPVs, so a given min_rrpv now protects roughly twice as long as it did when the i48/d32 depths were originally swept. This descriptor exists to re-find the optimum on the fixed machine; do not compare its numbers to any pre-fix td_* run.
_traces_dir: The local directory containing all simpointed traces
_top_simpoint: Run only top 3 simpoints stored in 'workloads_top_simp.json'.
_simulations: Post-fix re-sweep of the COMBINED marked-RRPV policy on the L2 (--td_combined_on_mlc 1: instruction lines take an RRPV from the L1I fetch miss's front-end-bound fraction via the td_fe_rrip_* knobs, data lines from the demanding load's membound fraction via the td_load_rrip_* knobs; each class keeps its own depth and threshold). Three axes. (1) DEPTH SCALE: depth_i*d* walks the (instr,data) minimum RRPV down the historical 3:2 ratio from the old tuned i48/d32 point to i6/d4. Since the aging fix doubled the effective protection at any given depth, the new optimum is expected around i24d16-i12d8 and i48d32 is expected to now OVER-protect (deeply negative lines squat in the set and the unprotected traffic thrashes the remaining ways). (2) CLASS ISOLATION: instr_only / data_only disable one class by raising its threshold to 1.0 (the qualification test is 'fraction > thresh' and a fraction cannot exceed 1.0, so nothing qualifies and every line of that class inserts at basic) -- this attributes the combined gain to the FE-bound or membound half. (3) GATE WIDTH: thresh_broad / thresh_narrow move both thresholds at the fixed centre depth, trading coverage against selectivity. extrap_i24d16 additionally checks the interpolated-ramp mode against the fixed-min mode used everywhere else. Compare IPC / MLC_DEMAND_MISS vs. the TPLRU baseline.
_configurations: NOTE: unlike the other td_* descriptors, 'baseline' here is NOT the untouched machine -- it is L2 tree-PLRU (--mlc_cache_repl_policy 21, REPL_PLRU_TREE), the realistic hardware reference that true-LRU flatters. true_lru (--mlc_cache_repl_policy 0) is kept as a separate config so the LRU->PLRU delta stays visible and so these numbers can still be lined up against the old TRUE_LRU-baselined sweeps. Every other config runs the combined policy; all of them hold --td_fe_rrip_extrapolate 0 / --td_load_rrip_extrapolate 0 (fixed-min mode) except extrap_i24d16. Naming: i<N>d<M> = --td_fe_rrip_min_rrpv -N (instruction class) and --td_load_rrip_min_rrpv -M (data class). CAUTION: --mlc_cache_repl_policy is silently IGNORED whenever a td_*_on_mlc knob is set (memory.c picks REPL_MARKED_RRIP first), so the policy ordinal appears only on the two non-td configs and must never be pasted onto a td_ config.

baseline._params: REPL_PLRU_TREE (21) on the L2 -- tree-based pseudo-LRU, the realistic hardware reference. This is the baseline every other config is measured against.

depth_i48d32._params: Depth scale: instr -48, data -32 -- the pre-fix tuned point. Expected to over-protect now that aging is halved.

depth_i24d16._params: Depth scale: instr -24, data -16. Half the old depths -- the predicted new optimum, and the centre point for the class-isolation and threshold axes.

depth_i6d4._params: Depth scale: instr -6, data -4 -- shallow end, close to plain SRRIP behaviour. Brackets the optimum from below.

instr_only_i24._params: Class isolation: instruction class at -24, data class OFF (--td_load_replay_thresh 1.0 -- no membound fraction can exceed 1.0, so every data line inserts at basic). Isolates the FE-bound half of the combined gain.

data_only_d16._params: Class isolation: data class at -16, instruction class OFF (--td_fe_rrip_thresh 1.0). Isolates the membound half of the combined gain.

thresh_broad_i24d16._params: Gate width at the centre depth: lower thresholds (fe 0.6 / load 0.4) qualify more lines -- broader protection, more contention for ways.

thresh_narrow_i24d16._params: Gate width at the centre depth: higher thresholds (fe 0.8 / load 0.6) qualify fewer lines -- only the most stalling misses are protected.

extrap_i24d16._params: Mode check at the centre depth: interpolated ramp instead of fixed-min. Both classes extrapolate with anchor 0.5 -- a line below the anchor inserts at basic, and from the anchor up to fraction 1.0 the RRPV is interpolated toward the class minimum, so protection depth tracks how stalling the miss actually was.

_collect_stats: Stats collection settings for ./sci --collect-stats. configs: optional list of configuration names to collect (null or omitted = all configurations).
_visualize: Visualization settings for ./sci --visualize. WINDOW WARNING: the 'IPC' named here is the TARGET-ONLY figure (Periodic_Instructions/Periodic_Cycles). plot_stat_change_multi.py's --stat IPC is a DIFFERENT quantity -- it resolves to Cumulative_Instructions/Cumulative_Cycles, which under --full_warmup spans warmup + target (i.e. what scarab-infra calls IPC_total). To plot the target-only figure with that script, pass --stat 'Periodic_Instructions/Periodic_Cycles' explicitly. MLC_FILL_DIRTY is included because the mlc_fill_line fix corrects L2 dirty-bit bookkeeping and therefore changes writeback traffic; it is the stat that shows whether a regression is aging-related or writeback-related.
_mem: Memory scheduling and collection settings for Slurm jobs.
